source: paper1_isa_v5.pdf Section 3.4 and paper1_isa_supplement_v5.pdf Section S7 (Table S7, Fig. S6)
headline: The anti-alias filter is a FEASIBILITY GATE, not the top influence factor. The v4.1 ranking LPF > Tlog > excitation > noise level is retired.
notes: The gate is an over-aggressive LOW cutoff, not the absence of a filter. At 50 Hz and above identification converges without failure - and so does unfiltered logging. The failures are confined to the <= 20 Hz cutoffs.
50 Hz is the WORKING cutoff, not a lower bound to be exceeded. Raising it to 100 Hz makes things worse.
The design factors interact too strongly for any single additive ranking to hold.

per_cutoff.note: Suppresses the oscillatory dynamics near the natural frequencies and destroys the information in the one-step residuals; the cascade inner loop adds phase lag the filter cannot track.
No error value is reported at 20 Hz, deliberately - survivorship bias.

per_cutoff.label: No LPF
per_cutoff.note: Unfiltered logging converges, but at the highest error of any setting: 54% pooled median.

feasibility_gate.note: This threshold is a property of the dynamics, not of the estimator.

main_effect_spreads_pp.scope: among runs that converge at a usable cutoff (>= 50 Hz), median spread
main_effect_spreads_pp.ranking: Tlog (74 pp) > noise amplitude (30 pp) ~ excitation (29 pp) > cutoff (9 pp)

working_cutoff.note: Raising the cutoff past 50 Hz brings no benefit.

noise_composition_vs_cutoff.note: The noise composition accounts for about +17 pp and the cutoff for about 5 pp, so the two levels are not comparable.

no_filter_boundary.note: Without a filter a 20 ms cadence sits at 2.5-3.0x its noise-free error, above the 2x tolerance, so the safe no-filter boundary is 50 ms. Applying a >= 50 Hz filter brings 20 ms back inside tolerance.

transition_table.definition: ratio of the sensor-noise median error to the noise-free median error at the same Tlog
transition_table.tolerance_note: A ratio near 1x means the added noise is immaterial; 2x marks the onset of material degradation.
transition_table.omitted: Tlog = 1 ms is omitted: under NF the one-step-difference predictor is a trivial near-zero solution, so its NF baseline is ~0 and the ratio is undefined.

lpf_tlog_heatmap.omitted_reason: most of its runs fail to converge

own_best_comparison.note: LPF >= 50 Hz should be read as a precondition, not 100 Hz as an optimum.

cross_channel.source: paper Section 3.4 and supplement Section S6
cross_channel.definition: ratio of two pooled medians taken at the same cadence: the velocity-noise error over the tension-noise error, each pooled over 4 matched noise levels (0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5% of full scale) x 3 seeds x 10 plants (n = 120 per channel)
cross_channel.mechanism: The corrupted velocity measurement feeds the high-gain inner loop directly, and finite-difference amplification is worst at fine sampling. The mechanism is unchanged from v4.1; the magnitude and its Tlog dependence are new.

composite.note: Sub-additive interaction: the composite error lands at roughly half the sum of the two single-channel errors, and below the velocity-only error itself.

extreme_low_dose.note: Already catastrophic at one tenth of the lowest symmetric level.

cross_channel.saturation_caveat: Individual parameter errors saturate at the optimizer bound, so in heavily degraded cells (most of the Tlog <= 5 ms grid) the reported medians and channel ratios are LOWER BOUNDS on the true degradation.

noise_model.note: Additive, zero-mean, Gaussian, per measurement channel. Noise is added to the SENSOR channels only, never in the ODE right-hand side.
noise_model.bias: Static sensor bias is NOT swept. The argument is analytic: temporal differencing in the PEM residual cancels a constant offset exactly. The v4.1-era '<1.2 pp' measured claim was removed.

aliasing_caveat: At Tlog >= 50 ms the effective sample rate falls below the 50 Hz cutoff, so the first-order EMA filter acts as noise smoothing rather than strict anti-alias. The net effect is small and mixed.
